item: Thunder Bay district, Ontario, 2026: response and hosting costs of the city and nearby First Nations, beyond what the Indigenous Services Canada estimate covers.
Nova Scotia: wildfire costs of its Emergency Management Office, which reports floods and wildfires together.
Northwest Territories: how its 2023 emergency spending splits between evacuation, response and recovery. Only the parts it itemized are in the total.
Kingston, Newfoundland and Labrador, 2025: buildings destroyed. No count is published and satellite images could not measure them reliably.

Buildings that satellite images miss where no official count is published: Alberta 2023, Quebec 2023, Manitoba 2025, Kátł'odeeche First Nation 2023, band lands at Bush Creek East 2023, and Bradley Creek and Pear Lake in BC, 2026. Images taken long after a fire miss the most.
Repair costs of FortisBC (2023 and 2026), ATCO Electric in Jasper (2024), Nova Scotia Power (2023) and Newfoundland Power (2025).
Repair costs of highways in BC, Saskatchewan (Highways 106 and 167) and the Northwest Territories, and of CN and CPKC rail lines.
Disaster aid paid to households and businesses in Saskatchewan, BC, Nova Scotia and Newfoundland and Labrador: no wildfire totals are published.
Farm losses and the wildfire share of farm support payments.
Mill shutdowns beyond what national output data show.
Nova Scotia's total paid in $500 payments to households that had to evacuate in 2023.
Mental health care for evacuees, and medicines and clinic visits linked to smoke.
